newsitem.title: UK: PowerGen posts higher profits, sets share buyback.
newsitem.headline: PowerGen posts higher profits, sets share buyback.

text.p: British electricity generator PowerGen Plc posted higher pretax profits Thursday and said it would buy back up to 10 percent of its stock.

PowerGen said its six-month pretax profits rose 4 percent to 138 million pounds ($228 million), excluding an exceptional credit of 69 million pounds ($114 million) from the sale of its 21 percent stake in another regional power company.
Finance Director Peter Hickson said in an interview that the company planned to repurchase 10 percent of its shares, but he declined to give a deadline.
"We'll do it over the coming weeks, as and when the board feels it's appropriate. Clearly, we need to see a steady share price, and we need to determine when the moment is right," he said.

The buyback announcement came amid market speculation about PowerGen's strategy after its 1.95 billion pound ($3.22 billion) bid for regional power company Midlands Electricity Plc was blocked by regulators this year.
"We believe that, having reviewed our balance sheet, the share buyback offers the best deal for our shareholders," Hickson said.
